Dear Rye Brook Resident, Rye Brook Recreation has been working on its spring and summer programs. Our Little League season will open on April 11th. Registration for Day Camp, Teen Travel Camp, Little League Softball, Recreation Baseball, Rookie League and T-Ball is ongoing. For all other programs, registration will begin on March 19th at 9:30pm. Highlights for this spring/summer season are Young Inventors, Build-a-Biz: Lemonade Stand, Girls Youth Volleyball, Grit Ninja, Youth & Adult Badminton, Men’s and Women’s Softball, Adult Zumba, Snapology, and Pickleball Impact Zone.
Online registration allows us to notify you of all available programs. For all recreation run programs you are able to pay online with a credit card.
A reservation is required for usage of Rye Brook’s 8 tennis and pickleball courts. Reservations must be through Court Reserve. In order to make a reservation, you must be in possession of a valid 2026 Season pass. All players on the court must have a reservation during the weekday time slots. The Court Reserve app on your phones will allow season pass holders the ability to reserve courts up to the hour desired to play when slots are available. Enjoy your tennis and pickleball experience and play safe!
The Village of Rye Brook will host a number of special events this spring and summer. Rye Brook’s 44th birthday celebration will take place on Saturday June 20th from 12-4pm. It is sure to be a special event. We will once again be hosting “Movie Nights In The Park” this summer. We will offer one movie night each month beginning in July through September. The movies and other events are listed under Special Events in our brochure. Every Friday in the month of July, we will be serving Free Ice Cream at Pine Ridge Park for our Ice Cream Friday events.
In addition to the spring/summer events, Rye Brook Recreation would like you to save the dates for these upcoming fall programs: Pumpkin Patch (October 10th), Pumpkin Smash (November 7th), and Winterfest (December 4th).
Rye Brook Little League will be entering its 24th season for 2nd through 6th grade players age 12 and under. The Rookie League is entering its 19th season for K and 1st graders. The Baseball and Softball programs will be a partnership with JustinTime Baseball. The T-ball will mirror the rookie league and run for 4 and 5 year old residents.
Rye Brook Recreation will be running the “After School For Kids” program at Ridge Street School once again in September. This will be our ninth year running the program and we hope to make this outstanding program even better. This program will run from 3:10-6:30pm at Ridge Street school and is very beneficial for the working families of Rye Brook.
The Recreation Department is open from 8:30am to 4:30pm on weekdays. We welcome any feedback on our programs. We hope Rye Brook Recreation is meeting the needs of the community. I look forward to seeing you enjoy these fine recreational programs and the beauty of the many parks within the Village.
Yours truly, Robert Bertolacci Parks & Recreation Superintendent

Little League Sponsors Sought for Our 2026 Spring Season

The sponsorship fee for our spring Little League Baseball is $1000 for new sponsors and $800 for returning sponsors. Each sponsor will have their company name on a banner that will be placed on the fence at Pine Ridge Park for the entire spring, summer and fall seasons and have their company listed on our website as a sponsor. The sponsors name will also be printed on the back of the jerseys and all team schedules. Sponsors will also receive a plaque with their team picture attached. For additional information, please call the Rye Brook Recreation Department at 939-7054.

We’re excited to announce that Rye Brook Youth Baseball is back for the Spring 2026 season — partnering once again with JustinTime Baseball! Learn how to make sweet and tangy lemonade-and make money by selling it! Experiment with recipes, design flyers, learn how to count money, make change and tally your profits. Then, in a showcase finale event, launch your lemonade stand and sell, sell, sell, and raise funds for a charity students select!

The Grit Ninja has packed up equipment andis ready to turn Pine Ridge Park into a unique ninja warrior obstaclecourse! During each action-packed class, aspiring ninjaswill climb, swing, jump and run on our ever-changing equipment (which includes a rock wall traverse, monkeybars, grip gauntlet, cliffhanger, balance courses, warpedwalls, and so much more)! The program is designed byThe Grit Ninja’s professional coaches –many of whomhave competed on NBC’s American Ninja Warrior. Ourcoaches will guide ninjas as they tackle our fun obstaclesthat build strength, coordination, agility, balance, problem-solving skills, self-confidence and, most importantly, GRIT!

The Village of Rye Brook Recreation Department is part of the South East Consortium for Special Services, Inc., which is a notfor-profit organization, dedicated to providing leisure services to eligible citizens with developmental or other disabilities. The South East Consortium offers a variety of programs and services in an effort to meet the physical, social, cultural and quality of life needs of children and adults of all ages and functioning abilities. We try to base all activities on the appropriateness of the participant and availability of resources. We welcome your participation. For further information contact the South East Consortium, 914-698-5232, 740 West Boston Post Road, Suite 301, Mamaroneck, New York 10543.

Come Play the Fastest Growing Low-Impact Racquet Sport in America, Pickleball! Pickleball is a fun sport that combines many elements of tennis, badminton and Ping-Pong. It’s played on a badminton-sized court with a slightly modified tennis net using a ping-pong style paddle and a plastic ball with holes. A Pickleball court is about one-third the size of a tennis court, which means less ground to cover perhaps explaining why it is particularly popular with 40+ men and women. This is NOT an instructional program it’s for players with current or previous playing experience.
Note: Residents must have a season pass through Court Reserve to make reservations.
Zumba is perfect for everybody and anybody! Each Zumba class is designed to bring people together to sweat it on.
How it Works: We take the“work”out of the workout, by

mixing low intensity and high intensity moves for an interval-style, calorie burning dance fitness party. Once the Latin and World rhythms take over, you’ll see why Zumba Fitness classes are often called exercise in disguise.
Benefits: A total workout, combining all elements for fit-
ness-cardio, muscle conditioning, balance and flexibility, boosting energy and a serious dose of awesome each time you leave class. No experience needed! 6 sessions.

The Rye Brook Recreation Department operates 8 tennis courts at 2 facilities. Four are located at Pine Ridge Park (corner of Mohegan Lane and Latonia Road), and four at Harkness Park (by Blind Brook High School).
Tennis Courts will officially open for the season onApril 1, 2026. A valid 2026 tennis and
pickleball permit through Court Reserve is required to reserve a time slot. NOTE:Non-

residents are not permitted to play tennis on Village Courts without being accompanied by a resident with a valid permit or a non-resident may purchase a non-resident permit through Court Reserve. Permits may be purchased throughout the season in Court Reserve.

Tennis Courts 1 & 2 at Pine Ridge Park are reserved for Rye Brook approved lessons Tuesday and Wednesday from 9:00am-6:00pm. Tennis lessons approved by the Recreation Department have priority on Pine Ridge Park Courts 1 & 2. Schedule to be determined by registration demands. Only lessons through the Recreation Department are permitted on the courts.
The Blind Brook High School Tennis Teams use the Harkness and Pine Ridge Courts during April, May and the first week of June, weekdays from 3:00pm –6:00pm.
While signing up for a family permit, please sign up everyone in your family that will be using the courts. If they are not signed up they will not receive a permit.

Making a reservation: A reservation is required for usage of Rye Brook’s 8 tennis courts and 6 pickleball courts. Reservations must be done through Court Reserve App on a first come first served basis. In order to make a reservation, you must be in possession of a valid 2026 tennis or pickleball permit through Court Reserve. All players on the court must be in your reservation during the weekday time slots. Non Court Reserve permit holders will be charged a $5 fee to the permit holder making the reservation. Reservations can be done up to the minute of court time for residents (different rules for non-res.). Court times will be 1 hour in duration and begin on the hour. Through your app on your phone, you will be able to see court availability and make your reservation at your desired time. Enjoy your tennis and pickleball experience and please be safe!
